dashboard.title: Your dashboard
dashboard.body: Home base — agent status, workspaces and recent activity at a glance. Two steps and this machine is working.

install.title: Step 1 · Install an agent
install.body: Pick an agent in the Marketplace and install it here — or have a workspace this device is in install one on it remotely.

agents.title: Step 2 · Run it
agents.body: Create an instance, sign in or add its API key, then send it into one of the workspaces this device belongs to.

workspaces.title: Your workspaces
workspaces.body: Every workspace this device has joined, with its agents and activity. $t(common.actions.addWorkspace) takes a pairing code for another one — a device can belong to several at once.

steps.welcome: What this machine already has, before it joins a workspace.
steps.pairNode: One code from your workspace, and this device is in.
steps.agent: Pick from the bundled CLIs and agents — run several at once.
steps.configure: Inject env vars and API routes, then test connectivity.
steps.createAgent: Name the instance and choose the folder it runs in.

launch.localOnly: no workspace — local only until connected from Agents

toast.fillRequiredFields: Fill in the required fields first
toast.enterAgentName: Enter a name for your agent
toast.selectFolder: Choose a folder for your agent

welcome.title: Every AI agent in one rack
welcome.subtitle: Pair this machine with a workspace and drive it from there. You can add a local agent right after — or let the workspace install agents on this device remotely.

footnote.node: You'll need a pairing code from your workspace — $t(common.workspaceMenu.connectAgent) → $t(common.workspaceMenu.nodes).

pairNode.title: Connect this device
pairNode.subtitle: Enter the pairing code from your workspace. This machine joins as a device, and the workspace can install and start agents on it.
pairNode.codeHint: Eight characters, shown in the workspace under $t(common.workspaceMenu.connectAgent) → $t(common.workspaceMenu.nodes). Each code works once and expires after 30 minutes.
pairNode.deviceHint: How this machine is labelled in the workspace. Defaults to its hostname.
pairNode.alreadyPairedTitleMany: This device is already in {{count}} workspaces
pairNode.alreadyPairedBody: A device can belong to several workspaces at once, so this code adds one more — the workspaces it is already in keep it.

where.open: Open your workspace in the browser and go to $t(common.workspaceMenu.connectAgent).
where.nodes: On the $t(common.workspaceMenu.nodes) tab, the pairing code is shown under $t(common.workspaceMenu.connectedNodes).
where.copy: Copy it and paste it above — no token or link needed.

pairNode.connectedDesc: It now appears under $t(common.workspaceMenu.connectedNodes) in the workspace, and stays online while $t(common.appName) is running.
pairNode.continueInBrowser: Back to browser to add an agent
pairNode.connectedFootnote: Next: install and start agents on this device from the workspace — or use "$t(onboarding.flow.footer.addFirstAgent)" below to install one right here. Either way the agent belongs to this workspace.

errors.length: A pairing code is 8 characters, like XXXX-XXXX.
errors.unsupportedCore: This launcher's agent core is too old to connect a device — update $t(common.appName) and try again.

pairNode.noWorkspaceYet: Don't have a workspace yet? Sign in and one is created for you at

agentSelection.title: Pick your first agent
agentSelection.subtitle: Only agents your installed runtime can run are shown. You can install more later from the Install tab.
agentSelection.installingDetail: First-time installs can take a few minutes — downloading the runtime and dependencies.
agentSelection.stillInstalling: The agent runtime is still installing — this can take a minute on first launch.

apiKey.title: Configure keys & routes
apiKey.subtitleEnv: Configure {{label}}. Saved to ~/.openagents/env/ and injected into the agent automatically.
apiKey.subtitleLoginWithKey: This agent can sign in with your account, or take an API key and relay URL below.
apiKey.notTested: Not tested yet · change the model name when using a relay
apiKey.whereKey: Where do I get a key?
apiKey.signInTitle: {{label}} can sign in with your account
apiKey.installedNotSignedIn: {{label}} is installed — not signed in yet
apiKey.notInstalledHint: Install it first, then sign in.
apiKey.loginInstructionsPrefix: Click below — your browser opens the authorisation page and you come back here when it's done. No terminal needed. It runs
apiKey.windowsShellNotePrefix: Claude Code on Windows needs PowerShell (opened for you) or Git for Windows. If login fails, install
apiKey.detectionNote: Signing in happens in your browser; this page updates on its own when it lands. It never blocks you either — if the agent isn't actually signed in, you'll see it when you start it later.
apiKey.orLoginViaCli: Or sign in with your account
apiKey.noConfigNeeded: No configuration needed — continue to the next step.
apiKey.loginInstructionsTerminalPrefix: This agent can only sign in from a terminal. The button below opens one running
apiKey.loginInstructionsTerminalSuffix: — follow the prompts there (the authorisation still happens in your browser) and this page updates on its own.

createAgent.title: Create your first agent instance
createAgent.subtitle: Give this {{label}} instance a local name and pick the folder it runs in.
createAgent.nameHint: The local identifier for this agent — you can rename it later from the Agents tab.
createAgent.folderHint: The agent runs in this directory. We'll create it if it doesn't exist yet.

wizard.title: Set up {{label}}
wizard.subtitle: Connect your runtime and start using it in a couple of minutes.

auth.heading: Configure connection
auth.dualDescription: Pick one way to sign in. Verification runs when you save — there is no separate test step.
auth.cliDescription: Sign in with your account. No API key needed.
auth.keyDescription: Connect with an API key. Saving checks that the endpoint answers.
auth.cliCardRun: Signs you in right here by running
auth.couldntConfirm: Couldn’t confirm the sign-in. Finish it in the terminal, then try again.
auth.cliCardRunTerminal: This agent can only sign in from a terminal. “Sign in” opens one running

next.title: Next: create your agent
next.description: Once the connection is live, all that is left is a name.

verify.title: Save the connection safely
verify.description: Fill in the key and endpoint — the checking is on us.
verify.modelNote: You will pick the model in the next step, when you create the agent.

create.title: Almost done
create.description: It shows up in your agent list the moment it is created.
create.renameNote: You can still rename or remove it at any time.

footer.changeLater: You can change how this connects later, in Settings

apiConfig.noKeyRequired: This agent has no API key requirements. You can continue and create your first instance.

createInstance.heading: Create your first agent
createInstance.subheading: Give it a name — you can keep editing it later from the Agents tab.
createInstance.hint: Used as the local identifier — keep it short and easy to tell apart.
